title: Recirculating-ball steering gear: worm bearing preload and sector mesh adjustment (1976-77 Dodge W/D trucks)
summary: Army procedure for taking slop out of the steering box in the right order: worm bearing preload first (4-6 in-lb off center), then sector mesh (14 in-lb through center).
warnings: From the Army manual for the M880 (military 1976-77 Dodge W200/D200). Confirm a civilian truck has the same part before using a number.

steps.text: Wheels straight ahead. Disconnect and remove the steering gear (pitman) arm from the sector shaft.
Remove the horn pad to get at the steering shaft nut.
Turn the wheel all the way right, then back off slightly to relieve any binding.

Put an inch-pound torque wrench on the steering shaft nut and turn toward the left, reading the torque to keep it moving. Worm bearing preload should be 4-6 in-lb. Test well away from center: the sector has a high spot in the middle.

If it's out: loosen the adjuster locknut two turns, back the adjuster plug out one turn to remove all preload, then turn it clockwise until the reading is 4-6 in-lb. Hold the plug, tighten the locknut and retest.
Only with preload correct, set the sector mesh. Count the turns stop to stop and come back exactly halfway to center.
Go about a quarter turn off center, put the inch-pound wrench on the shaft nut and turn through the center high spot. The reading (preload plus mesh) should be 14 in-lb.
If it isn't 13-15 in-lb, loosen the lash adjuster screw locknut, adjust the screw in the side cover until the wrench reads 14 in-lb through center, tighten the locknut and recheck.
Wheels straight ahead, reinstall the steering arm and tighten its nut to 180 ft-lb.
